title: Lena and the Border
premise: August Hartwell, a burned-out private security contractor haunted by a botched extraction he can't remember clearly, is approached by a stranger claiming August once saved his life — a favor August has no memory of. The stranger's price: extract Dr. Lena Voss, a cryptographer defecting from a hostile state, before an international summit where her knowledge could tip the balance of power. As August moves her across borders, he realizes Lena may be deliberate bait, dangled by both sides to flush out a mole inside his own firm — and that the 'incident' that broke his sleep was engineered to make him the perfect deniable courier. In the end, August chooses truth over loyalty, exposing the mole and trading himself to the enemy's handlers so Lena can reach the summit alive, walking into custody with the one secret that keeps him breathing.
about_author: Rosalind Okonkwo is a former logistics coordinator for humanitarian missions who spent a decade crossing checkpoints in West Africa and Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose loyalties are tested by geography, drawing on the border towns she knows too well.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV: August. Insomniac Hartwell takes a routine protection job in Trieste, where a stranger named Marek buys him dinner and claims August saved his life in Sarajevo — a debt August doesn't remember. Marek leaves a burner phone and a name: Lena Voss. The beat is unease; the reader learns August's memory of 'the incident' has holes someone else may have cut.

chapters.title: Cargo with a Pulse
chapters.summary: POV: August. Pressured by his firm's director, Calloway, to take the Voss job as a favor-trading exercise, August meets Lena at a Rijeka safehouse: sharp, terrified, and oddly prepared for extraction. She hands him a drive she insists he never open. The emotional beat is wary professional trust forming under time pressure.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Crossing toward Slovenia by night train, Lena calculates odds while August sleeps in shifts — and notices their route matches, exactly, a plan she was shown during interrogation. Someone on their side fed it forward. The beat is creeping dread: rescue and trap are the same itinerary.

chapters.title: The Mole's Signature
chapters.summary: POV: August. An ambush at a fuel depot kills their escort but spares them suspiciously. August recognizes the attackers' comms discipline as his own firm's tradecraft. He opens Lena's drive against her wishes and finds not codes but personnel files — including his own redacted incident report. Beat: betrayal curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: What August Forgot
chapters.summary: POV: August, intercut with fragmented memory. Under a chemist's help in Ljubljana, August recovers the buried night of the incident: he was dosed, used as an unwitting courier, and his team died covering the trail. The favor was never Marek's — it was leverage, planted long ago. Beat: grief and rage fused.

chapters.title: Two Handlers
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Cornered in a border town, Lena reveals she was permitted to defect — she's bait for the mole, run by her own service, and she's been playing both sides to reach the summit and burn the network from a podium. August must decide whether she's ally or instrument. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made explicit between two liars.

chapters.title: Calloway's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: August. August confronts Calloway, who admits the firm sold routing data to the hostile service years ago — and that August's broken memory was the price of August staying employed. Offered partnership in the lie, August records the confession instead. Beat: the quiet horror of institutional rot.

chapters.title: The Long Night at the Border
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Hunted by both services after the recording leaks partially, August and Lena run the final stretch through marshland toward the summit city, betrayed by a local fixer, wounded, and forced to split the drive's copies between them. Beat: exhausted devotion — they trust each other now because there's nothing left to hide.

chapters.title: Bait Takes the Hook
chapters.summary: POV: August. At the summit perimeter, August lets himself be captured by the hostile handlers, feeding them a false version of the drive while Lena reaches the podium with the real files. His interrogation becomes a stall; every minute she speaks, the network burns. Climax beat: sacrifice as strategy, fear held in check by purpose.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV: Lena, then August. Lena's disclosure detonates the mole network; Marek, revealed as her handler all along, honors the old debt by extracting August from custody before transfer. Weeks later, August sleeps through a whole night for the first time since the incident, testifying in exchange for leniency. Final beat: truth costs everything except the self.
